problem: The shift sentence reads "Shift: >; >>> is arithmetic right shift for signed values." The left-shift and logical-right-shift operators are missing from the text, so only ">>>" is defined even though the figure and worked example use "a << 1". A student cannot learn <<, >>, >>> from this line.
fix: Shift: << is logical left shift, >> is logical right shift, and >>> is arithmetic right shift (sign-extending) for signed values. Example: 4'b0011 << 1 = 4'b0110; 4'b1000 >>> 1 = 4'b1100 for a signed operand.

problem: The sentence reads "Relational  >= and equality == != return 1-bit", with a blank where the operators should be. The relational operators <, <= and > are never defined, yet > is used in the figure and worked example, so the operator set the exam tests is incomplete.
fix: Relational <, <=, >, >= and equality ==, != return 1-bit 0 or 1 (x if an operand bit is x or z). Case equality === and !== also match x and z.

problem: "Reduction: & | ^ ~& ~| ~^ before one vector return one bit" uses "before" where it means "applied to"; the wording is unclear on the phone.
fix: Reduction: & | ^ ~& ~| ~^ applied to a single vector return one bit. For example, &4'b1111 is 1.
